subject: Post-call: Pilot evidence kit — recommended models, TPS & latency links
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Morales <ethan@lumina.health>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 2 Jun 2024 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Pilot evidence kit — recommended models, TPS & latency links

Hi Ethan — thanks for taking time today. Quick recap + what I promised to share.

High-level takeaways from today:
- Primary use case: real-time Q&A over patient intake forms + summarization at ~2k token windows.
- Target SLO: p95 latency < 250ms for single-turn user queries; pilot throughput target ~150 TPS (burst to 300).
- Success criteria: answer accuracy >= baseline model (you provided), <5% hallucination rate on a 200-sample prompt set, and stable latency under typical traffic.

What we are sharing (attached + links):
1) Recommended model slate (Redwood-verified):
   - redwood-v3-medium-8bit (best latency/cost balance for RAG & summation)
   - redwood-v3-large-q4 (higher quality, ~2x cost, higher mem)
   - open-compat-2.1 (fallback; smaller but very low latency)
2) Benchmark evidence pack (attachments + Drive): TPS snapshots, latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) collected on 2k-token workloads. See attached "lumina-benchmark-snapshot.csv" and the Redwood-verified PDF.
3) Prompt set + regression guardrails: "lumina-prompt-set-v1.md" with the 40 canonical prompts we used for QA + automated eval hooks for future regressions.

Quick numbers (from our lab run matching your env):
- redwood-v3-medium-8bit: 150 TPS sustained, p95 = 210ms, p99 = 360ms
- redwood-v3-large-q4: 95 TPS sustained, p95 = 320ms, p99 = 620ms
- open-compat-2.1: 280 TPS sustained, p95 = 160ms, p99 = 290ms

Next suggested steps:
- Agree pilot scope (target 2-week run; traffic profile: 40% read, 60% summarization).
- Confirm which model(s) to include in pilot and pilot SLAs.
- Share legal/procurement contacts if you want us to draft a pilot MSA + PO path.

Deliverables I attached/linked: benchmark snapshot CSV, prompt set, and Redwood-verified performance profiles PDF. Marcus will follow up with a short runbook showing how we collected the TPS traces and how to reproduce locally.

If you’re ok, I’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff for Tue or Wed next week to lock pilot params.

Thanks — Sofia

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 3 Jun 2024 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Pilot evidence kit — recommended models, TPS & latency links

Hi Ethan — quick technical clarifications on the numbers Sofia shared. Thanks for flagging.

The 620ms p99 for redwood-v3-large-q4 was observed in a mixed-batched throughput run (batch size distribution peaked at 8 to simulate concurrent users) and included KV-cache warmups for long summaries. In single-request (no batching) profiling with an isolated GPU and the same 2k token window we see:
- redwood-v3-large-q4 single-request p95 = 310ms, p99 = 420ms (not 620ms)
- redwood-v3-medium-8bit single-request p95 = 200ms, p99 = 350ms

Notes and mitigation options:
- If Lumina prioritizes tight UI latency for reads, run the pilot with redwood-v3-medium-8bit for reads and redwood-v3-large-q4 for asynchronous summarization jobs.
- We can enable strict single-request execution and reduce batching to prioritize p99 latency at the cost of throughput; Marcus can show the config.
- For smoke test at 250–300ms target on reads: we recommend running redwood-v3-medium-8bit with max_batch_size=1 and a reduced concurrency profile (target 50–80 TPS) to validate client-side latency.

Repro steps & links:
- Repro runbook (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-lumina-pilot-pack (see folder "runbooks/repro-instructions.md").
- Redwood verified profile snapshot (attached PDF) shows both batched and single-request traces.

I attached a small CSV with the run slices we used; happy to schedule a 45-min technical kickoff with your infra lead.

—Marcus
